::: {#exr-miller-dint-order-of-integration}
#### Choosing the order of integration

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.48.

Evaluate the double integral:

$$\int_0^6 \int_0^5 x e^{-xy}\,dy\,dx$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-dint-order-of-integration}
Integrating with respect to $x$ first requires integration by parts. Integrating with respect to $y$ first is much simpler because the factor of $x$ is already present:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^5 x e^{-xy}\,dy
&= \sb{-e^{-xy}}_{y=0}^5 \\
&= 1 - e^{-5x}
\end{aligned}
$$

Now integrate with respect to $x$:

$$\ba
\int_0^6 (1 - e^{-5x})\,dx &= \sb{x + \frac{1}{5}e^{-5x}}_0^6
\\
&= \paren{6 + \frac{1}{5}e^{-30}} - \paren{0 + \frac{1}{5}}
\\
&= \frac{29}{5} + \frac{e^{-30}}{5}
\ea$$
:::
